tldr: The original Horvitz--Thompson finite-cohort ATE contrast has all-policy minimax precision regret of order \(q\log(1+Tq)\) under armwise every-prefix deficits and \(q^2\log(1+T)\) under individually bounded deficits, uniformly over finite horizons and shrinking radii. A single total, finite-computable anytime design uses only assigned outcomes, needs neither radius nor horizon, and has exactly zero regret at the unit-energy null. Cumulative positivity of signed reciprocal objectives and a prefix-repaired empirical-comparator converse deliver the two-class frontier. At radius \(1/4\), the unit-class converse also gives a logarithmic all-policy lower bound on the normalized Noarov class, complementing its published nearly logarithmic upper. The prefix and Noarov classes remain incomparable. Exact finite minimax calibration beyond the proved boundaries remains open.
